block.statement: The coach's face is the Gist kiosk (macmail/kiosk): one full screen and one exchange at a time. The founder sees only the prompt; a send plays the release; three balls bounce while the coach thinks; the reply lands with a flash and condenses in line by line. A status line and /wall stand in for the post-it wall. Name, email and consent are asked one screen each at the end. Steps 1-4 and the Socratic rules are unchanged.

At the end of the coach, after name, email and consent, the founder is shown their roadmap on screen as a kiosk tour: their product, problems, workarounds, jobs and features, then a first flight plan from Ground Zero that the coach cuts from their wall with one more model call, held to the release rules by check(). The emailed report is still the facilitator's run, seeded from that same plan.

The coach's last screen is the founder's roadmap website: the plugin coach's whiteboard page rebuilt in v2 words (web/roadmap.ts), opened over the kiosk from the tour's last screen, with Escape or back returning into the flow. Its v1-only sections are replaced by v2 versions: the trace (problem to workarounds to jobs), stories sized per release, what each release ships, would they pay for it, and the conversation as the log.
options_closed: the plain report page as the last screen

block.statement: The coach sends its own email through the smtp container's Postfix relay as db@zero2one.ee: a note to the facilitator for each finished conversation, and to founders who said yes the docs/emails series, 01 (their roadmap website) as soon as the flight plan is cut, then 02-04 after 3, 4 and 4 days, each with a stop link. Only conversations finished after mail was switched on are mailed.

COACH ACCOUNTS ARE BY EMAILED CODE AND NOTHING A FOUNDER MADE IS DELETED (2026-10-24, db). A founder proves their email with a six-digit code sent from noreply@zero2one.ee (15 minutes, 5 tries, rate-limited, stored only as a hash) and stays logged in for a year by an httpOnly cookie whose token the server keeps only as a hash; there are no passwords. Nobody has to log in to start: the code is asked at the end, and verifying it makes the account. A conversation with an account answers only to its login, except the emailed links /roadmap/<id> and /stop/<id>. Wall items and whole conversations are trashed and brought back, never deleted: the coach's remove tool trashes too, with what hangs off the item.

GROUND ZERO IS ARGUED DOWN BY THE FOUNDER IN THE CONVERSATION, NOT HANDED TO THEM (2026-10-24, db). Step 5 of the coach: the founder picks one job; the coach, as the visiting table, asks of each of its features whether they could still get the job done and still pay without it, pushes back once on a habit keep, and records the founder's keep-or-later with their reason; the founder names the month. The flight-plan cut takes that Ground Zero as given: exactly that job, that month, and exactly the features kept.

A team's screens stay in step by polling: every 3 seconds, GET /api/session/<id>?since=<n> returns the view only if it changed (a counter on the session), else 304. There is no live typing or presence: the room talks out loud.

One turn at a time per conversation: anyone in the team may answer; a second POST /api/turn while one runs gets 409 busy naming who is answering, and the other screens show <name> is answering… while their input waits.
